summary: Philippe Stern worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He held posts at the Musée Guimet (1927–1965), the Musée de la parole et du geste (~1928–1940), and the École du Louvre (1929–1965).

Philippe Turenne specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and McGill University (PhD, attested 2010) under G. Victor Sōgen Hori, Richard P. Hayes, Palden Sherab, and several other teachers.

Philippe-Édouard Foucaux was a scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies who studied under Eugène Burnouf. He held professorships at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales, the University of Paris (~1862–1894), and the Collège de France (1870–1894).
Phillip Bloom specializes in history, archaeology, and Sinology. He completed his PhD at Harvard University under the supervision of Eugene Y. Wang, Yukio Lippit, and James Robson.

Phra Brahmapundit is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He served as Chief Abbot of Wat Prayurawongsawat (~1996), Rector of Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (~1997–2018), and President of the International Association of Buddhist Universities (~2007).
Phra Khantipalo was a Buddhist studies and religious studies figure who studied under Jianmin Chen. In 1978, he served as abbot at Wat Buddha Dhamma.
Phra Maha Singhathon Narasabho studied Buddhist studies and philosophy. He completed his PhD at Visva-Bharati University under the doctoral supervision of Sudhindra Chandra Chakravarti.
Phra Medhidhammaporn studied Buddhist studies and philosophy. He completed his doctoral thesis in 1985 at the University of Delhi under Margaret Chatterjee and Mahesh Tiwary.

Phra Rajavaramuni studied philosophy at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University and education at Sukhothai Thammathirat Open University. He was attested in 2012 as Dean of the Faculty of Buddhist Studies and Deputy Vice Rector at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University.

Phra Sigambhirayan is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He earned a Bachelor of Liberal Arts at Sukhothai Thammathirat Open University and an M.A. in Buddhist studies at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University.

Phramaha Somphong Santacitto is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a master's degree in Buddhist studies at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University under the supervision of Phra Suthithammanuwat (attested 2006).
Phramonchai Saitanaporn is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He earned a Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Sydney under the doctoral supervision of Edward Fitzpatrick Crangle, attested in 2009.

Phuntsok Tashi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned a BA at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and an MA at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, and held a post at the National Museum of Bhutan.

Phyllis Granoff, a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies, earned her BA at Radcliffe College and PhD at Harvard University. She was a professor at McMaster University (~1976–2004) and was appointed at Yale University in 2004.

Pierre Bourdieu studied at Lycée Louis-le-Grand, Lycée Louis-Barthou, and the École Normale Supérieure, studying under Émile Benveniste. He held posts at the Faculty of Arts of Paris, Lille University, EHESS, and the Collège de France (1981–2001).
Pierre Chantraine was a linguist who studied under Antoine Meillet and Joseph Vendryes between ~1920 and ~1927. He later held a post at the University of Paris from ~1938 to 1969.

Pierre-Sylvain Filliozat worked in Indology and linguistics. He held posts at the French Institute of Pondicherry, École française d'Extrême-Orient, the Chair of Sanskrit at EPHE (1967–2004), and served as Vice-President of the Société Asiatique (2000–2019).
Pieter Cornelis Verhagen is a scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and linguistics. He completed his Ph.D. at Leiden University in 1991, where he was also attested as a research fellow in 1996.
Pieter Hendrik Pott worked in Indology, Tibetology, and history and archaeology. He served as a curator at Museum Volkenkunde (~1940–1965) and held a post at Leiden University in 1973.

Pietro Merlo was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Turin under Giovanni Flechia and Giovanni Maria Bertini. From 1877 he taught at the University of Pavia, becoming ordinary professor in 1885.
